subject: Scale and fallback behavior — discovery recap & test ask
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@brightlayer.com>, Ravi Shah <ravi@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Scale/fallback notes + asks (BrightLayer)

Hi Elena / Ravi — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap of the operational constraints and the items we promised to follow up on: 

- SLO targets you stated: p95 end-to-end latency <= 350ms for non-streaming inference; streaming chunk latency target ~< 250ms per chunk with max 1s recoverable tail behavior.
- Expected baseline throughput: 400 RPS sustained for normal traffic patterns; peak bursts up to 5k RPS (multiple short spikes, ~30–90s).
- Concurrency mix: ~60% short requests (<=128 tokens), ~40% longer streams (avg 512 tokens).
- Acceptance criteria for scale test: during a staged burst we maintain p95 <=350ms and no more than 2% of requests hit queueing fallback for longer than 5s.

Action items we committed to: 
1) Redwood to propose a warm-pool sizing and fallback queueing approach that meets targets (see attached warmpool-sizing.xlsx).
2) Book a 2-hour staged capacity run with production-like payloads (you suggested a maintenance window May 10 or 11).
3) Confirm telemetry we need from BrightLayer (sample IDs, typical token distributions, and a short list of critical endpoints).

Attachments: warmpool-sizing.xlsx (xlsx) — draft sizing + assumptions.

Next step: if the sizing looks sensible to you, can we lock May 10 09:00–11:00 PT for the staged burst run? If May 11 is better, we can do that as well.

Thanks — Naomi

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Scale/fallback notes + asks (BrightLayer)

Thanks Naomi — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

- Latency targets: Agreed on p95 <=350ms for non-streaming. For streaming we're focused on chunk-level responsiveness: average chunk RTT should be <200–250ms; we can tolerate occasional 600–1000ms chunk tails for long-form streams but want to measure how often those tails occur.
- Burst behavior: our spikes historically ramp to 4–6k RPS within ~20–60s, rarely sustained longer than 2 minutes. We need Redwood to demonstrate automated scale-up to cover the first 90–95% of that spike without degradation. The remaining 5–10% can hit queued fallback provided SLOs are preserved for core traffic.
- Warm pools: we're comfortable with a warm pool approach but prefer that prewarmed capacity be limited to 100 large-inference slots (we need to understand cost).
- Queueing fallback: on overflow we expect requests to be queued with exponential backoff and a 5s soft timeout before failing to downstream retry logic.

Telemetry we can provide: a 48-hour sample of production traces (anonymized), token distribution CSV, and two representative endpoints (query and streaming-chat). I'll drop links to those after I confirm with our infra team.

Yes to the May 10 window. Please send a one-page test plan and the list of payloads you want to run so we can greenlight infra.

Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Ops, BrightLayer
elena@brightlayer.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed test plan and queueing fallback (BrightLayer)

Internal-only note (do not forward to customer yet).

Thanks for the heads-up, Naomi. Based on BrightLayer's clarifications, here's a pragmatic plan that balances cost and SLO coverage: 

- Warm pool sizing: provision 80 prewarmed large slots (equivalent to ~80 GPU-backed inference instances) plus an autoscale buffer that can add another 200 instances in ~35–60s. We can run two variants during the test: 80-prewarm and 120-prewarm to show trade-offs. (See warmpool-sizing.xlsx).
- Fast-path routing: route shortest requests to a hot prefix cache and continuous batching lane to keep p95 low for core traffic. Streaming requests go to a dedicated streaming worker pool to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Queueing behavior: implement a leaky-bucket queue with exponential backoff and per-route soft-timeouts at 5s. For the staged run, instrument a histogram for queue wait times and percent of requests hitting queue >5s.
- Scale-in/scale-out test: start at baseline 400 RPS, then ramp to 5k RPS over 60s, hold for 90s, then decay. Run both prewarm variants and capture p50/p95/p99 for non-streaming and chunk RTT distribution for streaming.
- Fallback policy demo: show that critical endpoints (login, transactions) are pinned to hot pool instances and will not be queued; everything else follows queueing policy.

Deliverables for May 10 run: test script (we'll upload to the shared Drive), expected SLAs per step, and a short runbook for BrightLayer infra to open required ports and share tokenized payloads. I attached a quick diagram of the queueing/fallback flow (queueing-diagram.png).

Questions for Naomi / Karthik / Marissa: 
1) Cost estimate: do we want to prepare a rough cost delta for BrightLayer comparing 80 vs 120 prewarmed slots?
2) Observability: we'll need request-level tagging from their side (request id + route) — can Naomi ask Elena for that payload sample this week?

-Jordan

- By Apr 28: Redwood sends final test script and two prewarm variants (80 / 120) + expected metrics dashboard link.
- May 10 09:00–11:00 PT: Staged run (ramp to 5k RPS, hold 90s, decay). Redwood will stream results live and post the telemetry to the shared Drive.
- By May 12: Redwood will provide a post-run report that includes p50/p95/p99 for non-streaming, chunk RTT distribution for streaming, queue wait histogram, and fallout rate (>5s queueing).

Quick clarifying notes: 
- Cost: Jordan will scope a high-level delta for 80 vs 120 prewarmed slots; this is a sizing + cost trade-off and we'll label it as a non-binding estimate for procurement.
- Telemetry tags: request id + route + stream-id are sufficient. If you can include a simple CSV mapping of endpoint -> criticality that helps us ensure critical endpoints are pinned.

Please confirm that the above timeline works and that we should proceed to schedule the run for May 10. Once you confirm, we'll lock the run in our calendar and send the Drive link with the test script.
